newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Battle Mountain takes Nuigini chair.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Battle Mountain takes Nuigini chair.

text.p: Gold miner Nuigini Mining Ltd, which is 50.4 percent owned by Battle Mountain Gold Co, said on Friday that Battle Mountain executives had been appointed to the positions of chairman and chief executive at Nuigini.
Nuigini said that the board had been restructured in response to "concerns with the direction and performance of the company."
The changes include Battle Mountain finance vice president Dennis O'Connell replacing Geoff Louden as Chairman and Battle Mountain executive Joseph Baylis replacing Ian Goudie as chief executive.
Nuigini said the new board had asked management to undertake a strategic review of the company with a view to maximising the value of the company's assets to shareholders.
"The Board has requested that management undertake a strategic review of the company and prepare a business plan with view to maximising the value of the company's assets for the shareholders."
The restructure follows after talks between Niugini and Battle Mountain Gold Co over a possible Battle Mountain takeover bid for Niugini foundered on the issue of price.
Niugini last month said that the potential takeover price of A$4.00 per share indicated by Battle Mountain was insufficient.
Battle Mountain has said it wants to increase its exposure to Lihir Gold Ltd. Niugini has a 17.15 stake in Lihir Gold.
The takeover bid was seen as an attempt by Battle Mountain to secure complete control of that Lihir stake.
Some newspaper reports have said Battle Mountain wants Niugini to sell its non-Lihir assets, but has been obstructed by the Niugini board up until now.
